proposal: The Mandate recommends that FEMA raise the per-capita damage indicator or adopt a deductible, that Congress set the federal share at 25 percent for small disasters rising to 75 percent for catastrophic ones, that the National Flood Insurance Program be wound down and replaced by private insurance, and that most DHS preparedness grants be terminated. status_summary: As of 2026-10-07 the administration has a published plan that moves in the Mandate's direction but has not implemented it. The FEMA Review Council created by EO 14180 (2025-01-24) approved its final report on 2026-05-07 (published on dhs.gov; the report text could not be opened, so its contents below come from CRS and NACo). Per CRS and NACo it recommends raising Public Assistance thresholds with inflation and adding minimum state spending before a declaration, replacing project reimbursement with lump-sum state grants (RAPID), tying federal cost shares to state preparedness on a sliding scale, moving the NFIP gradually to private insurers (a CRS In Focus of 2026-08-28 reads this as a voluntary take-out program for certain policies under existing authorities, a marketplace evaluation and continued Risk Rating 2.0 pricing, and quotes the Council as acknowledging that legislation would be required to implement NFIP reform), making FEMA smaller as a payer of last resort, and keeping the Emergency Management Performance Grant; it does not propose moving FEMA to Interior, and CRS and NACo say the larger changes need Congress and a phased rollout of two to three years. No rule, order or law implementing it was found: the Federal Register shows only routine inflation adjustments to per capita indicators (2026-04-28 and 2026-09-29), and the House committee advanced H.R. 4669 in September 2025 with no Senate companion. On grants, FEMA canceled the BRIC mitigation program in April 2025 (about 3.6 billion dollars), a federal judge ordered it restored in December 2025 and March 2026, and FEMA reopened applications on 2026-03-25 under new criteria.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14180 establishes a FEMA Review Council, with a report due within 180 days of its first meeting and a one-year term unless extended; CRS says later orders moved the report deadline to no later than 2026-05-29.
FEMA publishes a Federal Register notice of the establishment of the FEMA Review Council.

Executive Order 14239 sets a federalism policy for preparedness and orders a National Resilience Strategy, policy reviews and a federal functions framework; it contains no cost-share or per-capita threshold changes.
Secretary Noem says at a Cabinet meeting that DHS will move to eliminate FEMA; Semafor notes closing the agency requires an act of Congress.

FEMA cancels the Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities (BRIC) mitigation grant program, affecting about 3.6 billion dollars in projects (month known only; first of month used). A judge later orders it restored (December 2025 and March 2026).

DHS says FEMA will limit Disaster Relief Fund activity to immediate threats to life, health or safety during the funding lapse; roughly four days later FEMA releases about 5 billion dollars. E&E News reported on 2026-02-27 that funding for ongoing and legacy disasters had been halted and allocations of 100,000 dollars or more were under review.

FEMA opens applications for 1 billion dollars in new BRIC funding for fiscal years 2024 and 2025 after court orders from U.S. District Judge Stearns in a suit by 22 states and the District of Columbia; new rules end funding for hazard mitigation planning and cap awards per recipient.

FEMA notice sets the statewide per capita indicator for recommending cost share adjustments at 189 dollars for major disasters declared in 2026; a 2026-09-29 notice raises the countywide indicator under the same inflation-adjustment practice. No larger threshold increase, deductible or cost-share change was found.

The FEMA Review Council approves its final report, published on dhs.gov (the report PDF and FEMA's release returned HTTP 403, so contents are from CRS Insight IN12693 dated 2026-05-15 and NACo dated 2026-05-11): recommendations include inflation-adjusted Public Assistance thresholds, minimum state spending before declarations, a RAPID lump-sum block grant, sliding-scale cost shares tied to state preparedness, a gradual NFIP shift to private insurers, a smaller FEMA and keeping the Emergency Management Performance Grant. These are recommendations; the larger changes need Congress.

title: Shift disaster costs to states; wind down NFIP and most FEMA preparedness grants
uncertainties: The Council's final report (dhs.gov PDF) could not be opened in the latest check either: the dhs.gov address returned a client error through the fetch tool, an archived copy on web.archive.org was blocked, and the FEMA press release of 2026-05-07 also failed to load. The report text therefore remains unread. Its contents come from two Congressional Research Service products that were re-opened and read (the Insight IN12693 and the In Focus IF13302 of 2026-08-28 on the NFIP recommendations), plus NACo and a Maryland counties summary, which differ in detail (for example NACo's estimate of about 16 fewer major declarations a year and a 150,000 dollar individual payment are NACo's figures). An external retrieval reported page-level details from a browser copy of the report (a ten-recommendation structure with an implementation table indicating that the parametric Public Assistance replacement, the single Individual Assistance payment, the Hazard Mitigation Grant Program replacement, NFIP reform and the FEMA transformation need legislation, a per capita indicator reset from 1.94 to 2.99 dollars, a federal share of 50 to 75 percent tied to state performance, and no recommendation to abolish FEMA or leave DHS). These details are known only through that external retrieval and are not stated as verified; the CRS products opened in this run are consistent with the general direction (sliding cost shares, lump-sum state grants, a voluntary NFIP take-out program, legislation needed for much of it, a two to three year phased rollout) but do not carry those figures. CRS cites a news report that the Council backed off proposed staffing cuts, which was not verified; an earlier lead that FEMA lost about one-fifth of its staff by July 2025 also remains unverified. Whether any executive order, rule or guidance has implemented the report since 2026-05-07 was not found in a Federal Register search of presidential documents, and the external retrieval also reported finding no implementing DHS or FEMA document; the search budget ended before checking FEMA press releases or reporting from June to October 2026, so the absence of implementing action rests on a limited search. The BRIC cancellation date (April 2025) and court order months come from one PBS report without exact days. Stage 'proposed' is a judgment: the BRIC cancellation was operative for several months before the court order, so a reader could argue for in_progress. Searches run: FEMA Review Council final report; BRIC, preparedness grants and NFIP. Plus Federal Register queries for per capita indicators and FEMA presidential documents.
